b027: A deck presenting a Greek cultural heritage foundation to international donors, in Greek and English. Headlines at 46px, body at 18px, projected and also distributed as a PDF. Restrained and dignified.

Users are often in distress, so text must be legible at 16px minimum with WCAG AA contrast, the Cyrillic must be drawn rather than adapted, and we need at least four weights for clear hierarchy. b059: An illustrated annual report for a Japanese children's charity, in Japanese and English, that should feel hopeful.
b083: A deck for a Japanese climate advocacy group presenting emissions data to policymakers, in Japanese and English. b094: Packaging for a Vietnamese fair-trade coffee sold to fund a literacy programme. It is bilingual, and it should feel considered and quietly premium rather than charitable.

b123: A printed annual report for a Russian environmental foundation. It carries a lot of financial tables that need aligned figures, and it should read as accountable and serious.
b128: A printed supporter newsletter for an animal rescue charity. It should feel warm and personal, and the text runs long enough that it has to stay comfortable.
b146: A mobile app connecting Vietnamese volunteers with local projects. It should feel welcoming, and the Vietnamese labels need to stay clear at interface sizes.

b176: A printed storybook collection produced by a Greek children's literacy charity. It reads for long stretches so it has to stay comfortable, and the Greek should feel warm and inviting to new readers.
b187: A deck presenting programme evaluation results for a Greek NGO that should feel rigorous.
b189: A printed history of a Russian cultural foundation that should feel refined.
b190: The site for a Japanese community mental health charity that should feel gentle.

b192: The site for a Vietnamese heritage conservation trust. b204: Packaging for a water filtration kit distributed by an aid organisation that should feel practical and clear.
b206: A campaign site for an organisation exposing labour abuses. Headlines at 64px must feel like an accusation, body at 17px must stay WCAG AA compliant. b003: A mobile client for a Vietnamese developer community. It shows code snippets inline so it needs a monospace companion, and the Vietnamese interface labels have to stay clear at small sizes.
b004: A conference talk deck about a new open source library that should feel light and human.
b007: Packaging for a limited-run hardware development kit sold in Greece, labelled in Greek and English, and it should feel considered and premium.

b032: A printed handbook introducing programming to Russian-speaking beginners. It runs long and is read slowly, so it has to stay comfortable, and the tone should feel encouraging rather than intimidating.

b044: A printed reference manual for a Russian embedded systems toolchain, 500 pages at 9pt in Russian and English. b107: A Japanese textbook on distributed systems that should read as precise.

b119: A printed book on software architecture aimed at senior engineers. It is read in long sittings and carries frequent code listings, so the text face has to pair with a monospace and stay comfortable at length.
b141: A Russian book of essays arguing that most software is bad, and it should feel uncompromising.
b143: A Russian-language terminal emulator app that should feel stark.
b147: A mobile app teaching Greek schoolchildren to code. It should feel encouraging, and the Greek interface labels need to stay legible alongside the code snippets.

b175: The site for an open source project with a cheerful mascot, and it should feel welcoming to first-time contributors.

b197: A deck presenting a Vietnamese cloud platform's reliability record to enterprise buyers.
